verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents creating machines through its API and CLI, and publishes a machine-readable OpenAPI spec and the pspace CLI for programmatic resource management, so the provisioning step is directly covered. The rest of the lifecycle is not explicitly evidenced: there is no documented API or CLI step for monitoring a machine, running a workload, or deleting/tearing it down. The DigitalOcean MCP servers are not shown to expose Paperspace tools, and high-end GPUs such as the H100 need human approval. Missing for 10: documented API/CLI monitoring of machine status and GPU metrics, documented programmatic workload execution, documented API/CLI machine deletion/teardown, a Paperspace-specific MCP toolset, independent hands-on corroboration of an end-to-end agent run.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can provision a GPU, monitor it, run a workload, and tear it down end to end through documented APIs, CLI, or MCP without a human in the console

citations.quote: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
Programmatically manage Paperspace resources using conventional HTTP requests.
Programmatically manage resources using the Paperspace Command Line Interface.
The production API domain serves a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0.3 document at /v1/openapi.json
